name: agent-browser
description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents
readmeExcerpt:
# agent-browser Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell.

agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. `snapshot` returns the page as compact text with a ref such as `@e1` for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one short shell call. ## Install ```bash npm install -g agent-browser agent-browser install # download Chrome for Testing (first time only) ``` - **Homebrew:** `brew install agent-browser`, then `agent-browser install`. - **Linux:** `agent-browser install --with-deps` also installs the browser's system libraries. - **No install:** `npx agent-browser open example.com`. Project installs, building from source, `upgrade`, and `doctor` are covered in [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation). ## Quick start ```bash agent-browser open example.com agent-browser snapshot -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-browser click @e1 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-browser get url # check the result agent-browser close ``` The snapshot for `example.com`: ``` - link "Learn more" [ref=e1] ``` - Refs describe the page at the time of the snapshot. After navigation or a DOM change, take a new snapshot before using refs again. - CSS selectors, text, XPath, and semantic locators also work, for example `agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit"`. See [Selectors](https://agent-browser.dev/selectors). - A click fails, instead of reporting success, when the target is hidden, disabled, outside the viewport, or covered by another element such as a consent banner. Dismiss the covering element, take a new snapshot, and retry. The full walkthrough is in the [quick start](https://agent-browser.dev/quick-start). ## How it works The CLI sends each command to a background daemon that starts on the first command and controls the browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Each `--session` gets its own daemon and browser. By default, the daemon closes a headless browser and exits after one hour without commands, saving state first when [session persistence](https://agent-browser.dev/sessions) is configured. Chrome for Testing is the default browser. You can also attach to a running Chrome with `--cdp` or `--auto-connect` ([CDP mode](https://agent-browser.dev/cdp-mode)), select the [Lightpanda](https://agent-browser.dev/engines/lightpanda) or [Obscura](https://agent-browser.dev/engines/obscura) engine with `--engine`, drive Mobile Safari in the [iOS Simulator](https://agent-browser.dev/ios), or use a cloud browser provider such as [Browserbase](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browserbase), [Browserless](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browserless), [Browser Use](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browser-use), [Kernel](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/kernel), or [AgentCore](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/agentcore). ## For AI agents The CLI ships skills that match its version: ```bash agent-browser skills get core # the core loop, refs, waiting, and common workflows agent-browser skills get core --ref commands # one reference, such as the full command list agent-browser skills get core --full # adds the full command reference and templates agent-browser skills list # specialized skills: electron, slack, dogfood, and more ``` Install the discovery skill into an agent harness from [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-browser): ```bash npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-browser ``` The installed skill is a thin stub that tells the agent to load `agent-browser skills get core`, so its instructions always match the installed CLI. Or add this to your `AGENTS.md`: ```markdown Use `agent-browser` for browser automation. Before the first use, run `agent-browser skills get core` and follow it. ``` For MCP clients, `agent-browser mcp` starts an MCP server over stdio. See [MCP server](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#mcp-server). ## Commands Run `agent-browser --help` for the full list, or `agent-browser --help` for one command. | Group | Commands | Docs | |---|---|---| | Navigate and read | `open`, `back`, `forward`, `reload`, `read`, `snapshot`, `get`, `is` | [Core](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#core), [Snapshots](https://agent-browser.dev/snapshots) | | Interact | `click`, `dblclick`, `fill`, `type`, `press`, `keyboard`, `hover`, `focus`, `select`, `check`, `uncheck`, `scroll`, `drag`, `upload`, `mouse`, `find` | [Core](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#core), [Find elements](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#find-elements) | | Wait | `wait` | [Wait](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#wait) | | Capture | `screenshot`, `pdf`, `record`, `download`, `diff` | [Recording](https://agent-browser.dev/recording), [Diffing](https://agent-browser.dev/diffing), [Files](https://agent-browser.dev/files) | | Page and network state | `cookies`, `storage`, `network`, `set`, `clipboard`, `eval`, `pushstate` | [Network](https://agent-browser.dev/network), [Settings](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#settings) | | Tabs, frames, and dialogs | `tab`, `frame`, `dialog` | [Tabs and frames](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#tabs-frames) | | Debug and performance | `console`, `errors`, `highlight`, `inspect`, `trace`, `profiler`, `vitals`, `react`, `a11y` | [Debugging](https://agent-browser.dev/debugging), [Profiler](https://agent-browser.dev/profiler), [React](https://agent-browser.dev/react) | | Sessions and auth | `session`, `state`, `auth`, `profiles`, `confirm`, `deny` | [Sessions](https://agent-browser.dev/sessions), [Security](https://agent-browser.dev/security) | | Agents and integrations | `skills`, `mcp`, `webmcp`, `flow`, `chat`, `batch`, `plugin` | [Skills](https://agent-browser.dev/skills), [WebMCP](https://agent-browser.dev/webmcp), [Plugins](https://agent-browser.dev/plugins) | | Observe | `stream`, `dashboard` | [Streaming](https://agent-browser.dev/streaming), [Dashboard](https://agent-browser.dev/dashboard) | | Setup | `install`, `upgrade`, `doctor`, `connect`, `close` | [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation) | Flags, environment variables, and `agent-browser.json` are documented in [Configuration](https://agent-browser.dev/configuration). ## Platforms Native binaries ship for macOS (ARM64, x64), Linux (ARM64, x64, glibc and musl), and Windows (x64). The npm package picks the right binary for the host. ## Development Building from source requires Node.js 24 or later, pnpm 11 or later, and Rust: ```bash pnpm install pnpm build:source # builds the dashboard and the native CLI pnpm link --global agent-browser install ``` Run the Rust checks from `cli/`: ```bash cargo fmt -- --check cargo clippy cargo test cargo test e2e -- --ignored --test-threads=1 # launches real headless Chrome ``` [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) lists the files to update with each change, the docs checks, and the release process. ## Documentation - [agent-browser.dev](https://agent-browser.dev): introduction, guides, and reference - [Commands](https://agent-browser.dev/commands) and [Configuration](https://agent-browser.dev/configuration) - [Security](https://agent-browser.dev/security): the auth vault, domain allowlists, action policies, and content boundaries - [Next.js and Vercel](https://agent-browser.dev/next) and [eve](https://agent-browser.dev/eve): running agent-browser in Vercel Sandbox and eve agents - [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) ## License Apache-2.0

releases.name: v0.42.0
releases.body:
### New Features

- Added **saved flows** (experimental): record a browser task once, then replay its requests. A run tries direct HTTP first, then the same request from the page, then a replay of the recorded commands, and saves the tier that worked. Runs send requests only to public addresses, and saving waits for in-flight requests and follows redirects to the end (#2236, #2397, #2432, #2433, #2444)
- **MCP tools** now list only the shared arguments each tool uses (#2311)

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed **session reuse and relaunch**, now decided in one place in the daemon. A connection target is kept only after an attach succeeds, and security settings persist across daemon restarts (#2396, #2418, #2429)
- Fixed **Safari and iOS WebDriver sessions** being dropped (#2385)
- Fixed **fill and type** altering literal text, and **mouse and element coordinates** losing fractional values (#2394, #2393)
- Fixed **percent-encoded proxy credentials** not being decoded (#2389)
- Fixed **downloads** moving local files from an attached Chrome (#2392)
- Fixed **MCP tool results** that repeated JSON stdout (#2390)
- Fixed **unknown commands and cookie operations**, now rejected, and **misplaced glob

releases.name: v0.41.2
releases.body:
### New Features

- Added **targeted skill references** with `skills get <name> --ref <ref>` and the MCP `agent_browser_skills_get` tool's `refs` argument, so agents can load one reference or template at a time (#2310)
- Added **Chrome security warnings** when newer stable releases list CVE fixes, without blocking commands. Set `AGENT_BROWSER_NO_VERSION_CHECK=1` to skip the check (#2309)

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed **session restarts** when commands omit or change timeout settings, preserving open pages and reusing the running daemon's default timeout for waits (#2288)
- Fixed **bare `open`** dropping configured profiles and browser arguments and relaunching Chrome with a temporary profile (#2287)
- Fixed **browserless commands** starting a browser when launch options are set in the environment (#2309)
- Fixed **Windows home directory detection** to respect `USERPROFILE`, and kept the MCP tool catalog's line endings consistent for Windows tests (#2305)

### Improvements

- Slimmed **the core agent skill** and routed detailed guidance to references, with instructions to pass `--session` on every command (#2303, #2312)

### Documentation

- Simplified **the README**, moved detailed guid

releases.name: v0.41.1
releases.body:
### Bug Fixes

- Fixed **cookie attributes** so `cookies set` honors `--http-only` and `--same-site`, preserves the existing aliases, and rejects unknown arguments (#2256)
- Fixed **page error clearing** so `errors --clear` removes captured errors (#2253)
- Fixed **MCP selector waits** so bare integer selectors return an error instead of becoming timed waits (#2254)
- Fixed **plugin error redaction** so sensitive operations omit unsupported protocol values (#2255)
- Fixed **invalid limit handling** so overflowing idle timeouts and invalid output limits produce warnings instead of overflowing or being silently ignored (#2250, #2258)
- Removed **unpinned npx execution permission** from the installed agent skill (#2249)

### Documentation

- Documented **stdin MCP connections** that reuse one server process in Vercel Sandbox (#2248)
- Configured **desktop documentation routes** and the desktop sitemap for the docs site (#2278)

### Contributors

- @Railly
- @lahfir

releases.name: v0.41.0
releases.body:
### Breaking Changes

- **`@agent-browser/eve` tools now come from the MCP tool catalog.** The extension exposes the CLI's MCP tools instead of 21 hand-written ones, so tool names and inputs change: `navigate` is `open`, `evaluate` is `eval`, `press_key` is `press`, `select_option` is `select`, `set_checked` is `check` and `uncheck`, `get` is `get_text`, `get_url` and the other `get_*` tools, `tabs` is the `tab_*` tools, and `wait_for` is the `wait_*` tools. The same names apply to `@agent-browser/eve/tools` overrides. The sandbox needs agent-browser 0.41, which the extension installs by default (#2241)

### New Features

- Added **`agent-browser mcp call <tool> '<json>'`** to run one MCP tool without a stdio session and print its result as JSON with the agent-browser version, for runtimes that cannot keep a process open between tool calls (#2238)
- Added **`@agent-browser/sandbox/mcp-tools.json`**, every MCP tool with its title, description, input schema, annotations and profiles, generated from the CLI and checked by a test (#2240)

releases.name: v0.40.0
releases.body:
### Breaking Changes

- **`@agent-browser/eve` now requires eve 0.84.0 or later.** eve 0.84.0 rejects extensions built by earlier releases, so the extension is now built with it. Apps on older eve should stay on `@agent-browser/eve@0.39` (#2226)

### New Features

- Added **one MCP server per Vercel Sandbox** with `startAgentBrowserMcp` in `@agent-browser/sandbox/vercel`, which keeps a single `agent-browser mcp` running over Sandbox stdin, and `connectAgentBrowserMcp` for any runtime that exposes stdin and stdout streams (#2228)
- Added **`--omit-command`** to `batch` and `omitCommand` to the MCP batch tool, replacing repeated raw command arrays in JSON output with zero-based indexes (#2216)

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed **`state load` and launch-time storage restores** exposing saved tokens to page scripts and writing one origin's storage into another after a redirect; storage is now written through DevTools only while the page is on the saved origin, and skipped origins are reported (#2212)
- Fixed **`<session>.config` files** piling up in the socket directory after daemons exit (#2128)
- Fixed **mocked cross-origin responses** failing CORS: `network route --body` now takes `--allow-o

agent-browser

Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell.

agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. snapshot returns the page as compact text with a ref such as @e1 for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one short shell call.

Install

npm install -g agent-browser
agent-browser install           # download Chrome for Testing (first time only)
  • Homebrew: brew install agent-browser, then agent-browser install.
  • Linux: agent-browser install --with-deps also installs the browser's system libraries.
  • No install: npx agent-browser open example.com.

Project installs, building from source, upgrade, and doctor are covered in Installation.

Quick start

agent-browser open example.com
agent-browser snapshot -i       # interactive elements, each with a ref
agent-browser click @e1         # act on a ref from that snapshot
agent-browser get url           # check the result
agent-browser close

The snapshot for example.com:

- link "Learn more" [ref=e1]
  • Refs describe the page at the time of the snapshot. After navigation or a DOM change, take a new snapshot before using refs again.
  • CSS selectors, text, XPath, and semantic locators also work, for example agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit". See Selectors.
  • A click fails, instead of reporting success, when the target is hidden, disabled, outside the viewport, or covered by another element such as a consent banner. Dismiss the covering element, take a new snapshot, and retry.

The full walkthrough is in the quick start.

How it works

The CLI sends each command to a background daemon that starts on the first command and controls the browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Each --session gets its own daemon and browser. By default, the daemon closes a headless browser and exits after one hour without commands, saving state first when session persistence is configured.

Chrome for Testing is the default browser. You can also attach to a running Chrome with --cdp or --auto-connect (CDP mode), select the Lightpanda or Obscura engine with --engine, drive Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator, or use a cloud browser provider such as Browserbase, Browserless, Browser Use, Kernel, or AgentCore.

For AI agents

The CLI ships skills that match its version:

agent-browser skills get core                 # the core loop, refs, waiting, and common workflows
agent-browser skills get core --ref commands  # one reference, such as the full command list
agent-browser skills get core --full          # adds the full command reference and templates
agent-browser skills list                     # specialized skills: electron, slack, dogfood, and more

Install the discovery skill into an agent harness from skills.sh:

npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-browser

The installed skill is a thin stub that tells the agent to load agent-browser skills get core, so its instructions always match the installed CLI. Or add this to your AGENTS.md:

Use `agent-browser` for browser automation. Before the first use, run
`agent-browser skills get core` and follow it.

For MCP clients, agent-browser mcp starts an MCP server over stdio. See MCP server.

Commands

Run agent-browser --help for the full list, or agent-browser <command> --help for one command.

Group Commands Docs
Navigate and read open, back, forward, reload, read, snapshot, get, is Core, Snapshots
Interact click, dblclick, fill, type, press, keyboard, hover, focus, select, check, uncheck, scroll, drag, upload, mouse, find Core, Find elements
Wait wait Wait
Capture screenshot, pdf, record, download, diff Recording, Diffing, Files
Page and network state cookies, storage, network, set, clipboard, eval, pushstate Network, Settings
Tabs, frames, and dialogs tab, frame, dialog Tabs and frames
Debug and performance console, errors, highlight, inspect, trace, profiler, vitals, react, a11y Debugging, Profiler, React
Sessions and auth session, state, auth, profiles, confirm, deny Sessions, Security
Agents and integrations skills, mcp, webmcp, flow, chat, batch, plugin Skills, WebMCP, Plugins
Observe stream, dashboard Streaming, Dashboard
Setup install, upgrade, doctor, connect, close Installation

Flags, environment variables, and agent-browser.json are documented in Configuration.

Platforms

Native binaries ship for macOS (ARM64, x64), Linux (ARM64, x64, glibc and musl), and Windows (x64). The npm package picks the right binary for the host.

Development

Building from source requires Node.js 24 or later, pnpm 11 or later, and Rust:

pnpm install
pnpm build:source               # builds the dashboard and the native CLI
pnpm link --global
agent-browser install

Run the Rust checks from cli/:

cargo fmt -- --check
cargo clippy
cargo test
cargo test e2e -- --ignored --test-threads=1   # launches real headless Chrome

AGENTS.md lists the files to update with each change, the docs checks, and the release process.

Documentation

  • agent-browser.dev: introduction, guides, and reference
  • Commands and Configuration
  • Security: the auth vault, domain allowlists, action policies, and content boundaries
  • Next.js and Vercel and eve: running agent-browser in Vercel Sandbox and eve agents
  • Changelog

License

Apache-2.0

aiSummary.oneLiner: A headless browser environment specifically optimized for AI agents to navigate, scrape, and interact with the web.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Agent Browser provides a specialized, headless web browsing environment tailored for AI agents rather than human users. It strips away unnecessary visual rendering overhead, focusing instead on exposing a clean, structured DOM representation that language models can easily parse and manipulate. The tool translates complex JavaScript interactions and dynamic content into standardized tool calls, allowing agents to reliably click, type, and scroll. It handles CAPTCHAs, authentication states, and dynamic loading autonomously, ensuring robust scraping and automated interaction. This enables developers to build web-fluent agents without fighting brittle traditional testing frameworks.
keyFeatures: AI-optimized DOM parser: Converts complex, dynamic web pages into a simplified, semantic representation easily digestible by LLMs.
Autonomous state management: Automatically handles session cookies, authentication flows, and anti-bot mechanisms like CAPTCHAs.
Action translation engine: Maps natural language agent commands into precise, reliable browser interactions like clicking and typing.
Headless execution environment: Runs efficiently without a GUI, minimizing resource consumption during large-scale automated scraping.
Dynamic content resolution: Waits for asynchronous JavaScript execution and network requests to settle before feeding data back to the agent.
Extensible middleware system: Allows developers to inject custom logic for specific site scraping or specialized interaction patterns.

useCases.title: Automated data extraction
useCases.description: Deploy an agent to navigate complex, dynamically loaded e-commerce sites to extract pricing and product details reliably.

useCases.title: End-to-end workflow automation
useCases.description: Instruct an agent to log into a SaaS platform, navigate specific dashboards, and export data reports without human intervention.

useCases.title: Intelligent web testing
useCases.description: Use LLMs to autonomously explore a web application, identifying broken flows and UI inconsistencies dynamically.

useCases.title: Research and summarization
useCases.description: Have an agent search the web, click through multiple pagination links, and synthesize the collected information into a single report.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: AI developers and data engineers building agents that require robust, autonomous web interaction capabilities. It replaces brittle, traditional scraping tools with an intelligent, LLM-native browsing environment.
